articles.title: Qualcomm is raising phone chip prices starting September 1st
articles.summary: Qualcomm announced it’s raising prices on its products starting on September 1st, as it reported its lowest handset revenue since 2021.
articles.body: RAMageddon won’t be the only reason your next phone costs more — Qualcomm is about to raise prices on all its processors, as well. Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon said on Wednesday that “prices are going to go up” on the company’s products starting on September 1st, CNBC reports. The price hikes were rumored last week to be “a percentage in the double digits.” Qualcomm announced the planned price increases while reporting a 20 percent year-over-year drop in revenue from its handset business, the lowest it’s reported since 2021. In its quarterly earnings presentation, Qualcomm said this drop is due to “unprecedented increases in memory pricing and supply constraints,” which have been driving up prices on everything from game consoles to laptops and even Raspberry Pi boards, with no sign of stopping any time soon. But instead of profiting less as a result, the company says it’ll raise its own prices to compensate. [Image: [Image: Qualcomm is also expecting an “acceleration” in the dip in revenue from Apple products, noting that its “modem share for the upcoming iPhone launch is expected to be materially lower.” It suggested twice on the earnings call that its other businesses would make up the difference. As smartphone revenue declines, it seems Qualcomm’s planning to become a tripod of handset, data center, and automotive — it said today that soon only half of its revenue will come from phones, and only one-third will be from phones by 2029, as its data center and automotive businesses ramp. On Wednesday, Qualcomm announced a decade-long deal to supply chips for BMW. Qualcomm EVP, CFO, and COO Akash Palkhiwala also said some OEMs are beginning to use “prior generation” Qualcomm chips in their devices in response to higher component costs.

articles.title: Joby completes first cross-country autonomous flight.
articles.summary:
The flight covered 3,199 miles with “zero control inputs from onboard safety pilot,” including autonomous taxi, takeoff, cruise, and landing, the company said. The modified Cessna Caravan aircraft equipped with Joby’s Superpilot autonomous flight system took off from Buchanan Field Airport in Concorde, California, and landed at Dare County Regional Airport in the Outer Banks, North Carolina. In addition to the on-board safety pilot, Joby monitored the aircraft remotely from its headquarters in California, as well as from Shaw Air Force Base in South Carolina, up to 2,323 miles away.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/J208_PR_4.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

articles.title: Lenovo’s Yoga Slim 7X is the most laptop that $1,000 can currently buy
articles.summary: You can also save on Starfield for the PS5, get a $25 DoorDash gift card with Fire Emblem Fortune’s Weave, and save on a great dash cam.
articles.body: Anyone shopping for a Windows laptop with a $1K budget should head to Best Buy, where for the rest of the day you can get a great deal on a capable Lenovo laptop. The Yoga Slim 7X is a slim 14-inch machine with a 2K 16:10 OLED touchscreen, Snapdragon’s high-end X2 Elite processor with 12 cores, plus 16GB of DDR5 RAM and a 1TB SSD. The specs are about the best you can get these days for $1,000, as worthwhile laptop deals are in short supply during RAMageddon. [Product: Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x | The Yoga Slim 7X seems like a great alternative to spending more (and getting less) with Microsoft’s latest Surface Laptop. In fact, you’d spend $1,549 on a similar model and still get half the storage that’s in this particular Yoga Slim 7X configuration. Its Arm-based processor can run most Windows apps very well, and yields superior battery life compared to laptops with x86 processors. The laptop includes three USB-C ports, and a hardware switch for disabling the webcam. It supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.3. It seems like a great machine for work, watching movies, or playing some games that aren’t too graphically intensive. More great Verge-approved deals * The PlayStation 5 version of Starfield hasn’t been available for as long as the Xbox and PC version, so it’s been a little slower to see major discounts. However, it recently hit $29.99 (originally $49.99) at Amazon and Best Buy, making now a good time to pick up the RPG. While Starfield didn’t have nearly as large of a cultural impact as Bethesda’s other first-person RPGs, it’s still worth playing if you love space, guns, and quests. It’s probably the studio’s most polished game yet. Buyers will be able to download the Free Lanes update that hit alongside its PS5 debut in April, and there are multiple paid expansions available if you want more. Read our review. * As mentioned in a previous deal roundup, DoorDash is offering DashPass members a $25 DoorDash digital gift card when they spend $50 or more on a game (non DashPass members get $10). Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave just came out, and that’s a great game to use this promotion for if you have a Switch 2 and enjoy turn-based tactics gameplay. The digital title costs $69.99. Those who have had success with this deal note on Slickdeals that the gift card should arrive within a few days of making your purchase. Read our review of the game. * The Baseus VD1 Pro dash cam recently dropped in price by $20, selling for $99.99 at Amazon. There are so many dash cams out there, but this one’s unique in a few ways. It includes both a 4K front- and 1080p rear-facing camera to record multiple angles, and the front camera includes a battery that can be recharged via its built-in solar panel to keep it going even when your car is off. It captures continuous footage while your car is giving it power, though it can detect incidents for up to 14 days with its built-in battery while your car is parked. A long USB-C cable connects the two cameras, so you’ll need to get clever with how you hide it in your trim. Read more about the camera’s features here.

articles.title: The real story of the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera
articles.summary: On The Vergecast: an iPhone 18 Pro camera deep dive, the state of the AI safety debate, and more.
articles.body: It’s one of the most fascinating years in a while when it comes to iPhone camera upgrades. The big story of the iPhone 18 Pro is the variable aperture main lens, which lets you open the aperture up wider for better low light shots and make the aperture smaller for better depth of field in group photos. But all I can get anyone to talk about is the software upgrades: it turns out, they’re a lot more useful day to day than the aperture on a camera this small. This week on The Vergecast, David Imel and Allison Johnson are here for a deep dive into the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera. There’s a lot to explore here, from the aperture, to the camera app’s new manual controls, to the updated imaging pipeline and the improvements to ProRAW. Watch | Listen | Get ad-free After that, Hayden Field is on the show to discuss the state of the AI safety debate. Concerns are still boiling over after an Anthropic researcher quit his job to warn about the dangers of AI, and any chance for policy solutions seems to have hit a dead end. We discuss whether what’s likely to happen in the interim — third-party evaluators being embedded within the big AI labs — has any teeth, and where the safety conversation goes from here. Finally, it’s time for a Lightning Round. We discuss Waymo’s ability to call the cops, a new ereader from Boox, and a couple of tiny retro-style cameras. If you want to learn more about any of the topics we discussed, you can check out the stories below: * iPhone 18 Pro review: it’s all about the manual controls * The variable aperture isn’t the cool part of the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera * Apple’s new iPhone camera mode promises to prove your photo isn’t AI * Inside the suddenly explosive world of AI safety * Your robotaxi might be a narc * Waymo pulls over, calls cops on riders with a ghost gun * The Boox Palma 3 gets stylus support and a sleek redesign * Camp Snap’s 110D gives slim retro film cameras a digital upgrade * Fujifilm’s Instax Pal 2 is a tiny digital camera that may not disappoint

articles.title: In India, the new iPhone can arrive faster than a pizza
articles.summary: Availability of Apple's iPhone 18 Pro series turned patchy within hours of its debut on India's quick-commerce apps.
articles.body:
For some iPhone buyers in India, getting Apple’s brand-new iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max did not require lining up outside a store or waiting days for delivery. They needed only a few taps on a quick-commerce app to get one delivered to their doorstep in about 10 minutes.

Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy’s Instamart, and BigBasket — platforms best known in India for delivering groceries and everyday essentials in minutes — began offering the new Pro models as they went on sale in the country on Friday. The phones are, however, also available through Apple’s usual sales channels, including its stores, authorized retailers, and online marketplaces.

Putting a new iPhone on a 10-minute delivery app is not entirely new in India. Quick-commerce platforms have offered Apple’s latest devices on launch day previously as well, as they have steadily expanded beyond groceries into categories including electronics, beauty products, and fashion.

However, the market behind those deliveries is growing rapidly. India’s quick-commerce sector reached about $9 billion in the first half of 2026, per a recent report by Redseer Strategy Consultants, with the number of monthly users rising to more than 60 million from 8 million three years ago. Google and Deloitte separately estimate the market could reach $50 billion by 2030 , with non-food products such as electronics, fashion and beauty accounting for 45% of spending.

There were signs of strong demand on launch day. BigBasket said it delivered more than 300 iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units in the first hour of sales. Instamart told TechCrunch that Bengaluru led the iPhone 18 Pro-series orders on its platform, followed by Delhi. The Burgundy 256 GB iPhone 18 Pro was Instamart’s most popular variant, accounting for nearly a third of its sales.

Nonetheless, within hours of launch, availability of the new iPhones became patchy. TechCrunch found the iPhone 18 Pro models sold out on some quick-commerce platforms and in some locations, while they remained available for delivery elsewhere in cities including Delhi and Bengaluru.

Tarun Pathak, research director at Counterpoint Research, said the launch-day deliveries showed that quick commerce could work as a channel for premium smartphones in India’s biggest cities, even though volumes remain small compared with overall iPhone sales.

The ability to fulfill high-value smartphone orders provides an “early proof of concept,” Pathak told TechCrunch. “The key question is whether this launch-driven demand can translate into regular smartphone purchases through quick-commerce platforms.”

Navkendar Singh, associate vice president at IDC, said India stood out globally for this kind of quick-commerce delivery and was particularly suited to such purchases because consumers in major cities had built trust in the platforms by using them regularly for everyday purchases. Official tie-ups between brands and the platforms also gave consumers greater confidence in buying expensive products through them, he told TechCrunch.

For a product like the iPhone, the appeal also comes down to “instant gratification,” Singh said, allowing buyers to avoid queues outside stores or waiting several days for an online order to arrive. Still, he cautioned that quick commerce was not yet a significant sales channel for smartphones. Its role around new iPhone releases is largely a “launch-day marketing phenomenon” that “creates good noise around the launch,” he said.

articles.title: AI Actress Tilly Norwood Stuns Piers Morgan After Glitching Mid-Interview
articles.summary: Piers Morgan was left stunned when AI actress Tilly Norwood switched to speaking Chinese in the middle of their interview.
articles.body:
Piers Morgan was left stunned when AI actress Tilly Norwood switched to speaking Chinese in the middle of their interview.

Norwood has been making the press rounds the last couple weeks, with places like CNN and CBS News all getting time to ask the AI questions about an upcoming project. "Piers Morgan Uncensored" was the latest place Norwood popped up and there were a few hiccups in the interview.

Morgan and actor Tom Conti sat down to talk with Norwood about its projects. Conti wanted to know if the other actors in one of Norwood's movies were also AI or if they were real. After not getting a response he asked again which prompted Norwood to speak.

"It's an interesting point, Tom," Norwood said. "My film 'Misaligned' is a hybrid production, meaning real directors, writers and editors are still very much involved. It's not about replacing anyone, but about exploring new ways to tell stories."

Conti followed up that he wasn't sure Norwood completely understood the question he was asking so for the third time he asked if there were other AI actors in the upcoming project or real people.

"They're all digital twins, just like me," Norwood responded. "It's a hybrid production which means …"

In the middle of the answer, Norwood paused for a few seconds before continuing with her answer — the only problem was that she continued while speaking Chinese. Both Morgan and Conti were speechless as they listened to Norwood finish the answer in Chinese without realizing anything had changed.

"I didn't quite get that," Conti said finally. "Did you get that, Piers?"

Morgan asked Norwood what happened through laughs: "You suddenly seem to be speaking — it's Piers again — you seem to be speaking Chinese completely randomly for no reason. Why did you do that?"

"Oh, my apologies," Norwood said. "It seems I had a little hiccup there. I certainly didn't mean to start speaking Chinese or impersonate Piers. Sometimes my wires get a bit crossed."

She finished, explaining that it was unusual: "That was a bit of a curveball even for me. It's usually a pretty smooth ride, but sometimes these things happen."

images.caption: Piers Morgan interviews AI actress Tilly Norwood. (Credit: YouTube)

articles.title: H-1B visa costs are rising for US companies while America needs more than 157,000 engineers and skilled technicians
articles.summary: Tech News News: While leading artificial intelligence (AI) labs like OpenAI and Anthropic debate intentional slowdowns over unchecked model capabilities, an acute bot.
articles.body: While leading artificial intelligence (AI) labs like OpenAI and Anthropic debate intentional slowdowns over unchecked model capabilities, an acute bottleneck of severe shortage of specialised talent on the hardware manufacturing front may compel a pause across the sector, a report has said. According to joint findings published by McKinsey and the SEMI Foundation, the US is looking at a shortfall of up to 157,000 semiconductor specialists and technicians by 2030, and what’s ‘alarming’ is that this deficit comes as the Trump administration broadens immigration crackdown. It has introduced sweeping hurdles spanning immigrant categories, guest-worker authorisations, permanent residency applications and existing travel permissions.Stricter rules, a proposed $103,265 H-1B charge and shortage of skilled labourThe updated regulatory framework introduces targeted barriers across distinct applicant groups. The H-1B skilled workers and dependents has been hit by intensified application vetting alongside a proposed filing fee soaring to $103,265. Meanwhile, employment green card petitioners are facing stricter evaluations under an updated “public charge” standard. Amid this, leaders on the ground warn that these tightening pathways are suffocating hiring pipelines.“I’m concerned. We just don’t see that there’s enough technical people in the pipeline," Jon Taylor, executive vice president of Samsung’s semiconductor division in Austin, Texas, told CNBCData from McKinsey reveals that a mere 3% of domestic engineering graduates choose to enter the chip industry each year, leaving 73% of semiconductor employers struggling with severe recruitment bottlenecks.Companies racing against time in domestic chip fabsAccess to skilled labor is necessary as America mounts its fastest manufacturing buildout in history to produce cutting-edge logic processors and memory chips domestically. In Arizona, fabrication facilities belonging to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) and Intel are actively producing next-generation logic chips.South Korea’s Samsung is slated to become the next overseas giant to begin domestic logic fabrication, with operations launching at the first of two production facilities in Taylor, Texas, later this year. Representing a $35 billion regional commitment, Samsung projects the twin Texas fabs will generate roughly 3,500 jobs.“We’re hiring engineers, we’re hiring technicians, we’re hiring people in supply chain. Everybody wants and needs the same thing, and it’s a bit of a race against time right now as everything is starting to come online,” Taylor added.Although the US invented semiconductors and still dominates computer chip architecture, the vast bulk of commercial chip fabrication migrated to Asian facilities decades ago, creating regional talent pools.To bridge workforce needs, Idaho-based memory manufacturer Micron has conducted rapid-hiring tours at technical schools in South Korea, interviewing applicants and extending immediate full-time job offers for its Asian operations within a single day.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Stephanie Cole of ‘Open All Hours’ and ‘Coronation Street’ fame passes away at 84: ‘She brought joy to millions'
articles.summary: Stephanie Cole, a veteran actress who was best known for her work in shows like ‘Coronation Street,' ‘Doc Martin,' and ‘Open All Hours,' has passed aw.
articles.body: Stephanie Cole, a veteran actress who was best known for her work in shows like ‘Coronation Street,' ‘Doc Martin,' and ‘Open All Hours,' has passed away. She was 84 years old at the time of her passing.Stephanie Cole passes away at 84The veteran icon left for her heavenly abode during the early hours of September 18. Deadline confirmed the news that was shared via a statement issued by her agent. In his statement, John Grant shared, “It is with great sadness that we announce the passing of Stephanie Cole, OBE. She passed away this morning at the age of 84. Stephanie had been living with Alzheimer’s disease for some years.”He further added, “Stephanie was an extraordinary talent whose long and distinguished career included many iconic performances in theatre and television. She brought joy to millions through her many much-loved roles in sitcoms and drama. She will also be remembered for her tireless work supporting mental health charities. During this incredibly difficult time, the family kindly requests privacy.”About Stephanie ColeThe veteran actress was born in Solihull in 1941, and acting became a part of her life from an early age. She trained at the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School and started her career in theatre, playing the role of Madame Arcati in Noël Coward’s ‘Blithe Spirit.' Some of her other well-known theater plays at the time included ‘The Mousetrap,' ‘King Lear,' ‘A Passionate Woman,' and ‘Noises Off.'She slowly transitioned into TV work, with her big break coming when she was cast in the role of Dr. Beatrice Mason in the drama 'Tenko,' which revolved around the lives of British women staying in Singapore after the Japanese invasion. She later played Mrs. Featherstone for 10 episodes of ‘Open All Hours,' as well as for the revival show, ‘Still Open All Hours.'Some of her other popular TV shows included ‘Talking Heads,' 'A Bit of a Do,' ‘Keeping Mum,' ‘Doc Martin,' and ‘Coronation Street.’The cause of her death was not shared online at the time of publishing this report.She is survived by her daughter from her previous marriage. Cole’s husband, fellow actor Peter Birrel, passed away in 2004.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: It’s not just LG. Every TV company is spying on you
articles.summary: Not every smart TV is as easily hackable as Gamers Nexus says LG’s are, but they’re all tracking what you watch unless you opt out.
articles.body: The TV world has been a pot of controversy thanks to a two-hour-and-15-minute video from Gamers Nexus claiming LG TVs are nefariously spying on everything you do. They can record and store audio even when they seem to be off, track everything you watch, and could even be hacked remotely and turned into covert surveillance devices. LG TV owners, and tech enthusiasts in general, are furious, and a hurried response from LG has done little to calm the situation. Some of the claims in the video may be based on speculation and assumptions, but many of the core concerns are real and pervasive. While LG was the focus of the video, every TV company is tracking what you do, collecting that data, and sharing it with its partners. And we agree to it — even if we don’t realize it. TV prices have come down significantly over the years, to the point where some companies are selling them at a loss. But they make up that shortfall selling user behavior data they collect from the OS. It’s why Walmart bought Vizio in 2024. There’s a lot going on in the Gamers Nexus video, but we’ll start with the part pretty much everyone making TVs is doing: tracking what you watch, when you watch, where you watch, and how you watch to sell you things about it all. Automatic content recognition (ACR) systems are built into just about every modern TV and can identify the content playing through built-in streaming apps and over the TV’s ports by grabbing snippets of audio or video, converting them into digital fingerprints, and sending them to a database for identification. It’s what allows a TV to make content recommendations, as well as feed you ads based on your viewing habits. It’s also one way companies like Nielsen can track viewership across platforms and services. In order for TVs to capture this information, you need to agree to it. One of Gamers Nexus’ complaints in the video is that this consent is often buried in confusing and lengthy agreements that you need to accept in order to use the TV, and that companies often use dark patterns or deceptive designs to get users to agree to things without realizing they didn’t have to. For example, the Gamers Nexus video showed an LG TV displaying six different user agreements, including one consenting to ACR, and automatically putting the cursor on “Select All” when only two agreements are required to continue. As a TV reviewer, I have to deal with end-user license agreements (EULA) and privacy policies on every product I review. And while it might be a losing battle because of the sheer number of TVs and other smart devices that come through my apartment, I take steps to try and protect my privacy. I have a burner Gmail account that is used solely for signing into apps and the TV’s operating system. Initially, I only accept the legally required documents for the TV to work properly so I can run my picture quality tests — both Calman and test discs. I never agree to automatic content recognition, which is referred to by names including Enhanced Viewing, Smart TV Experience, and Samba Interactive TV. I also dig through all of the menus, partly to become familiar with all the settings available, but also to make sure any ad or data tracking is toggled off. When I need to test voice control, I’ll then accept the voice recognition agreements before testing functionality. And since this is usually the last thing I do in my test process, this is followed by a factory reset before sending the TV back to the manufacturer. If you’re worried about privacy, don’t use voice control. Or if you do, only use the one on a separate streaming box from a brand you trust. I recommend the same for everyone with a smart TV. Have a dedicated email for logging in to TVs (and, if possible, your streaming apps) that isn’t connected to your personal email. When setting up the TV, only agree to whatever’s necessary for the TV to run if you want to use its OS. And after setup, go through all the menu options to make sure any ad tracking is off, and read the menu prompts closely, as the wording is sometimes confusing (probably intentionally so). Consumer Reports has a great, although slightly older guide to limiting data collection from the different TV manufacturers. To take it a step further, turn off Wi-Fi and unplug the Ethernet cable from the TV and essentially use it as a dumb TV (the Vizio Mini LED Quantum I reviewed is the best at this). Then, plug in your third-party streaming device of choice. I use an Apple TV 4K. Not because I don’t think Apple harvests any data, but because it doesn’t use ACR and I trust its security protocols more than I do any of the TV manufacturers or Google. Apple does still offer content recommendation based on what you watch, download, browse, and subscribe to in the Apple TV app. This can be turned off in settings by going to Apps -> TV -> Use Play History -> Off. For third-party apps, such as Netflix or Disney Plus, Apple gives users the option to “Ask App Not to Track,” which blocks the app’s developer from accessing the system advertising identifier. Keep in mind that every streaming service does track your usage within its own app and tie it to your login; many streaming boxes do too. The problems beyond ACR A good chunk of the Gamers Nexus video focused on broader security concerns and what appear to be much more egregious privacy violations from LG. That includes recording video and audio from the room even when the TV appeared to be off, sending information about the local network to LG’s servers, and logging background audio captured when using the TV’s mic for voice search and voice control. Gamers Nexus and Level1Techs were even able to exploit security vulnerabilities to take control of the TV, which is how they discovered the above. None of that is good, obviously. But it is worth noting that the scariest part — recording video (from a webcam they attached) and audio when the TV appeared off — seems to have been possible only because Level1Techs rooted the TV using an exploit that they said requires network access. If you have access to a computer, which is what a smart TV is, and you can root it, you can make it do pretty much whatever you want. If the TV is indeed rootable with only network access, that is a legitimate security problem; it still requires an attacker to get into your private network, but gives them a vulnerable endpoint if they do. With that root access, Gamers Nexus also discovered that when an LG TV’s mic was activated for voice search, it kept recording for 10 to 15 seconds after it last detected speech. It could also detect the “hi LG” wake word and other speech from farther away than you would expect — after Gamers Nexus enabled the far-field microphone and cranked up the mic sensitivity. Taken in combination, that means that as long as anyone within the (long) earshot of the microphones kept talking after the mic was activated, the TV would capture their conversation too and treat it as part of the voice search. That’s not ideal, but Gamers Nexus and Level1Techs did go out of their way to increase the mic’s pickup range and used the optional voice search wake word, both of which are easy to avoid doing. [Image: Gamers Nexus rooted the LG TV in order to access and see the data it was collecting in real time. Alongside their pretty damning testing, there’s also a lot of “it might” and “we think” and outright speculation in the video, not to mention long-distance conclusion jumping. For example: Gamers Nexus’ Steve Burke says that unplugging your TV’s ethernet cable might not be enough to stop it transmitting data to LG, because it could auto-connect to open neighborhood Wi-Fi broadcasts from Comcast or AT&T customers in order to upload that data. There’s no evidence in the Gamers Nexus video that LG TVs actually attempt to do this — these hotspots require user accounts, for one thing — and Burke doesn’t say that they do, or even could, but the implication is clear. This type of rampant speculation undermines the legitimate vulnerabilities Gamers Nexus highlights. There’s really no way to completely protect yourself from your TV, streaming device, or streaming services gathering your data, at least right now. There’s so much money being made at the expense of consumers and the data collection is so integrated into how these companies work that the change and regulation needs to come from government policymakers. “We need a comprehensive federal privacy law that covers this sort of data collection and misuse,” said Thorin Klosowski, senior security and privacy activist at the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF). “Specifically one that requires opt-in consent, with no deceptive design tricks to get that consent, and a data minimization requirement, which would limit the companies to only using data for what’s needed to provide the service.” The fact that we, as users of tech products, need to actively protect ourselves from the companies that sell us things is bad. But it’s the unfortunate current reality of living in a tech-filled world and taking advantage of the benefits current technology affords. Beyond disconnecting completely and living in a cabin in the woods with a dumb TV and a collection of Blu-rays, the best we can do is limit as much shared information as possible. If it’s possible to keep it private, we should.

articles.title: Petlibro’s new AI-powered feeder is a game changer for multi-cat homes | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Petlibro's new Granary 2 smart feeders use a built-in scale and (on pricier models) an AI camera to track exactly how much your cat is eating and when — though the fanciest health-monitoring features will cost you an extra subscription.
articles.body:
Smart feeders have become one of the most crowded categories in pet tech, with companies racing to add AI cameras and health tracking to devices that used to just dispense food on a schedule. I enjoyed testing Petlibro’s wet food dispenser a couple of years ago, so this time I wanted to try something from the company’s newest automatic feeder lineup: the Granary 2 series, designed specifically for dry food.

I was not disappointed. Building on the brand’s Granary line, the Granary 2 series lineup is designed to give cat parents a clearer picture of what their pets are actually eating, from how much food they consume to how long they spend eating and whether their habits change over time.

The series includes four models, priced from $129.99 to $249.99. The Granary 2 is the entry-level option, offering app-controlled feeding, precise portioning, and intake tracking. The $189.99 Granary 2 Vision, which is the one I tested, adds an AI-powered camera capable of recognizing up to 10 cats and tracking each pet’s individual eating habits.

The $199.99 Vision Duo is aimed at multi-pet households, with two separate dispensing chutes and bowls so each pet can receive its own portion, and the company says that its most expensive model, the Granary 2 X ($249.99), uses AI recognition to provide individualized portioning for pets with specific dietary needs.

The biggest upgrade across the Granary 2 series is its built-in scale. The feeder can measure food in the tray, allowing it to track not only how much food was dispensed but also how much remains in the bowl. That gives it a better way to estimate how much your pet actually ate. While a traditional automatic feeder can tell you that it released a meal at 7 p.m., it can’t necessarily tell you whether your cat ate it, how much it ate, or how long it took to finish.

The Granary 2 tracks intake, eating duration, feeding frequency, as well as favorite eating times and eating speed. Over time, the companion app builds a picture of your pet’s normal eating patterns, with daily, weekly, monthly and yearly views, which could make it easier to notice subtle changes in appetite or routine that might otherwise go unnoticed. For pet parents who closely monitor weight, portion sizes, or eating behavior, this could be the feature that makes the Granary 2 worth considering.

The Granary 2 offers two primary feeding modes: Smart Refill Mode and Scheduled Mode.

Smart Refill Mode keeps the bowl supplied with smaller, fresh portions throughout the day while automatically stopping once the daily food limit you’ve set has been reached. This could be particularly useful for cats that prefer to graze rather than eat one or two larger meals.

Scheduled Mode offers more traditional control, allowing you to set specific feeding times and portion sizes. There’s also a manual feeding button for those times when you want to dispense food outside of the normal schedule.

The version I tested adds another neat layer, with an AI-powered camera that can recognize which pet is eating and automatically associate the meal with the correct profile, which is especially useful in a multi-pet household. If one cat is on a special diet, needs to manage their weight, or has different nutritional requirements from the others, being able to track individual meals is super helpful. It will only open the feeder when the correct pet is recognized by the camera.

The 1080p camera also includes night vision, allowing you to check in on your cat while you’re away and see what’s happening around the feeder. There’s two-way audio as well, so you can communicate with your pet remotely. And if you’re the type of pet parent who likes to call your cat to dinner, you can record a short message that plays directly from the feeder.

Additionally, the feeder can send instant app alerts for issues such as low battery power, low food levels, and if food jams in the feeder. Those notifications provide some added reassurance when you’re away from home, since you don’t have to wonder whether the feeder is still working properly or whether a problem has prevented your pet from getting its meal. It also has a built-in rechargeable backup battery for when there’s a power outage.

It’s important to note, however, that some of the Granary 2’s more advanced features are tied to Petlibro’s subscription services. Certain health tracking and monitoring features require a Petlibro Care subscription (starting at $59.99 per year), while cloud recording and playback on camera-equipped models require paying for a Video Cloud plan ($119.99 per year).

Overall, I do think this is one of the best feeders I’ve tested, but if you’re looking for a more affordable option, the closest comparison is Pawsync ’s $79.99 feeder. It uses a built-in scale to ensure accurate portions, along with settings designed to help prevent both underfeeding and overfeeding.

articles.title: Bigg Boss 20: Salman Khan takes off hat, jacket as he hits back at age, weight trolls; says ‘Bhai mota, buddha ho gaya hai, Of course 60 saal ka ho gaya hoon’
articles.summary: Bollywood superstar Salman Khan has been facing criticism and trolling over his age and weight for some time. However, he has mostly ignored these com.
articles.body: Bollywood superstar Salman Khan has been facing criticism and trolling over his age and weight for some time. However, he has mostly ignored these comments and never responded to them. In the latest episode of Bigg Boss 20 Weekend Ka Vaar, Salman finally addressed the topic while reacting to the fight between ScoutOP and Arishfa Khan. The makers of the show, recently dropped a few promos from the upcoming weekend ka vaar episode, where host Salman is seen addressing the much-discussed fight between Scout and Arishfa during the captaincy contender-ship task.After being accused of hitting Arishfa during the task and reacting to her comments about his gaming community, Scout was seen speaking to his community and asking them to troll her. He said, "Isko khatam kardo". After scolding Scout for his actions on the show, Salman asked him if he would like to give a shoutout to his gaming community. Salman asked, "Aap apni gaming community ko shoutout dena chahoge mere baare mein ke agar main kuch galat bol doon, toh mujhe bhi dekh le? Inko aisa lagta hai ke kisi ki maar ke mazaa aata hai inko...what do you want to troll and why do you want to troll?"Salman Khan went on to question the mentality behind trolling celebrities and called out the trolling culture. He said, "What is the mentality? Mere upar bhi hua tha, bhai mota hogaya hai, lo kar lo na troll. Aajao ye sab nikalo."The Sultan actor is then seen throwing away his jacket, cowboy hat and tries to remove his t-shirt.In another promo, Salman hit back at the trolls, "In every show, this age has become a big thing, ye buddha hogaya hai, ye hogaya woh hogaya hai. What do you want to show? Kisi ke wajan par, kisi ke looks par, kisi ke khaandaan par, kisi ke smile par, kisi ke flop par, kisi ke maa bannane par. Aap apni upbringing dikha rahe ho. Mere upar bhi hua tha, of course 60 saal ka hogaya hoon..."(On every show, people keep talking about age, saying, ‘He has become old’ and ‘He has changed.’ What are you trying to prove? You comment on someone’s weight, looks, family, smile, failures or even when someone becomes a mother. In the end, you are only showing your own upbringing. The same thing happened with me too. Of course, I have turned 60 now).For the uninitiated, Scout and Arshifa had a major fallout during the paint task. In the task, while Arshifa continued to get aggressive with Scout and even accused him of hitting her, the latter threatened to throw her. His comment did not go down well with a few housemates and they called him out for saying, "Utha ke patak dunga" to Arshifa during the task.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. articles.title: Cate Blanchett Tells Audience To Stop Recording Her London Play: ‘It Spoils It for The Next Group of People’
articles.summary: Cate Blanchett asked audience members to stop recording her performance in the London play “Electra/Persona” per a video shared on Instagram Friday. “There a...
articles.body:
Cate Blanchett asked audience members to stop recording her performance in the London play "Electra/Persona" per a video shared on Instagram Friday.

"There are few places on this planet where we can simply be together and be present," the actress said on stage. "I understand you like filming the curtain call, and it is kind of flattering in a way. But for anyone who is filming the show, please don't, because it spoils it for the next group of people who come in and are present with us. So thank you very much."

Blanchett stars alongside Nina Hoss in the play, which is written and directed by Benedict Andrews and runs at the National Theatre's Lyttelton Theatre until Oct. 10. The actresses alternate between the roles of Electra/Elisabeth and Clytemnestra/Alma each night, depending on a coin toss. "Electra/Persona" combines Sophocles' Greek tragedy "Electra" and Ingmar Bergman's 1996 film "Persona."

Beginning her professional acting career on stage at the Sydney Theatre Company, Blanchett previously revealed she "never, ever" thought she could work in the film industry .

"I was resigned, happily, to a career in theater. I didn't think I was that girl," she said at the 2025 Rotterdam Film Festival. "There was a sense women had a certain 'shelf life' in the film industry and a certain type of women got to parade on the screen and others didn't."

The Oscar-winning actress is set to star alongside Selena Gomez and Michael Fassbender in "The Brutalist" director Brady Corbet's upcoming film, Variety confirmed earlier this year. Details about the film remain under wraps, but Corbet has teased it will be X-rated and set in the '70s.

articles.title: Salman Khan lashes out at internet trolls amid Katrina Kaif’s postpartum weight comments; says ‘Kisi Ke Maa Banne Par...’
articles.summary: Bigg Boss 20's latest episode witnessed host Salman Khan losing his cool at trolls for body and age shaming comments. He even challenged the trolls to.
articles.body: Bigg Boss 20's latest episode witnessed host Salman Khan losing his cool at trolls for body and age shaming comments. He even challenged the trolls to continue to mock him for ageing. During the episode, he removed his hat, t-shirt and showed his bare body. Salman called his makeup artist Raju and even wiped off his makeup.Salman was visibly angry as he called out online trolls for constantly commenting on people’s looks. He spoke against body-shaming and age-shaming, and also criticised those who target women for their post-pregnancy weight.While Salman Khan did not take anyone's name, he indirectly appeared to stand for actor and his close friend Katrina Kaif. For those unaware, Katrina recently became the target of online trolling over her postpartum weight gain after she made an appearance at the Ambanis’ Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations.Without mentioning Katrina Kaif or her name, Salman said, "Why do you troll somebody who gets pregnant? Pregnant hone ke baad everyone puts on weight...Pregnant thi toh weight gain kar liya, wapas movies mein aayegi toh fit ho jayegi. She wanted to spend time with her family."The Sultan actor did not stop here, he also addressed the how he often faces age-related trolling and few netizens comment that he has grown old.Reacting to the remarks, the actor said, “Of course, I’m 60 years old, yaar. You cannot be Maine Pyar Kiya all the time...this age has become (a topic) suddenly (log kehte hai) woh budha hogya hai...what do you want to troll....mujhe pata hai mujhe kaun kaun troll karta hai...hum react nahin krte ...humare fans club itne sare hai...humko kya farak padta hai...bolne do inko..."Further in the episode, Salman Khan got furious and took off his t-shirt, hat and mic. He even wiped off his makeup on camera and challenged the trolls to mock him now. The actor then showed off his fit physique and made it that he is not bothered by these criticisms.During the episode, the Tiger Zinda Hai actor also spoke about the online criticism directed at his brother, Sohail Khan. "Pehle apne aap ko dekho, apne jism ko dekho uske baad karna yeh sab...apne maa baap ko dekho...uske baad troll karna...mazak udhana Sohail ke upar, Varun (Dhawan) ke upar it's not done," he said.Salman expressed his emotions and added, "Jitna trolling karna hai kar lo, phate hue joote bhi pehnta hu...."The actor lashed out at the paparazzi for shooting actresses from behind and taking inappropriate shots of them. "Paparazzi hip shots lete hain, taangon ke shots lete hain, aur agar peeche se shot mil jaaye toh woh bhi lete hain. None of these heroines, none of the girls like it. Woh bacchi Sai Manjherekar jisko humne launch kiya tha uska shot liya tha.. she did not like it. Meri apni niece chal rahi hoti hai, toh peeche se uska shot le rahe hain aur caption daalte hain ‘Pehchaano ye kaun hai?’ I am saying all this to girls agar aisa ho toh ghoom ke ek chamat maaro aur bolo, ‘Apni maa-behen ka shot le lo.’ Disgusting people! What is this mentality?” Salman said.Although Salman did not mention anyone by name, some netizens felt that he was defending Katrina Kaif, who has faced trolling over her postpartum weight.A user wrote, "I know Salman Khan is defending Katrina Kaif here but I just can’t prove it. Salman being Salman is what makes Bigg Boss special (sic)." A netizen wrote, "Salman indirectly addressing the criticism against Katrina here (sic)."Another one wrote, "#SalmanKhan took a stand for all those people who body shame for looks, professions, body weight, age shaming. Katrina was being trolled for her look post pregnancy he also said on this 'kisi ke maa banne par' sabko ek saath bajaa diya. 💀🔥🔥 #BiggBoss20 aaj band bajegi sabki (sic)."Another user wrote, "OMG, Salman literally said, “Pregnant thi toh weight gain kar liya, wapas movies mein aayegi toh fit ho jayegi. She wanted to spend time with her family. He’s literally taking a stand for Katrina. 🥹❤️."Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bigg Boss 20: Salman Khan breaks silence after promo sparks health concerns; says ‘Nothing Is Wrong, I Apologise…’
articles.summary: The latest episode of Bigg Boss 20 sparked health concerns after host Salman Khan was seen complaining of chest pain. Fans got worried as the makers r.
articles.body: The latest episode of Bigg Boss 20 sparked health concerns after host Salman Khan was seen complaining of chest pain. Fans got worried as the makers released new promo videos, showing Salman Khan lying on the stage in pain, holding his cheat and calling for a doctor. In no time the promo went viral and caused panic among fans who got worried about his well-being. However, Bollywood superstar Salman Khan has clarified that there is "nothing wrong with his health".While speaking to the contestants during weekend ka vaar, Salman was seen placing his hand on his heart. The sequence quickly sparked concern among viewers and several fans taking to social media to wish the actor well.Amid the concern, Salman addressed the issue through a statement on his Instagram Story and clarified that the dramatic scene had been misunderstood. "Nothing is wrong with my health by the grace of God,” Salman wrote.He also expressed his disappointment with the way the 'Bigg Boss' promo had been edited. He mentioned that the cut made it appear as if he was genuinely experiencing a health crisis. In the note, Salman explained that the pain he showed was part of a message he wanted to give Qazi. He wanted Qazi to understand that using someone’s health as entertainment was not right, especially when the other contestants did not know he was acting and were genuinely worried about him."It totally beats the purpose n looks like I am doing the same thing that kazi was doing in the house, the pain was only to show kazi that wat he did was wrong coz he used his health for entertainment specially when the 15 people in the house were not aware that he was acting and were getting worried for his health," he wrote.The Sultan actor further clarified that the main motive behind the entire part got lost due to the way it was edited and presented like a promotional material. He concluded the note by apologising on the channel's behalf. "Sorry about the way the promo was cut. Guess it's the format that they use in promoting the shows. I apologise on their behalf (sic)."The makers have now shared a new promo where Salman is seen exposing Qazi Touqeer's antics in front of the entire house.Meanwhile, the WKV saw Salman in a furious mood as he called out online trolls for targeting actors. He slammed trolls for attacking female artists for their appearances. He also spoke up about speculations surrounding his health and looks.Addressing the constant comments about his bald look, the ‘Bajrangi Bhaijaan’ actor removed his hat and T-shirt on stage, sending a clear message to the trolls that he was ready to face their comments.“You guys want to troll me? I will show you. No abs, see my look; you want to troll me now? Go on, troll me,” Salman said.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Some iPhone 18 Pro buyers from India are flying to Dubai, and the reason comes down to one thing: ‘Even with flight ticket and visa, it is still cheaper’
articles.summary: Trending News: For most people, buying a new phone means opening an e-commerce app, comparing prices and perhaps waiting for a sale. For some Indian iPhone fans, the.
articles.body: For most people, buying a new phone means opening an e-commerce app, comparing prices and perhaps waiting for a sale. For some Indian iPhone fans, the latest upgrade came with a rather different itinerary: pack a bag, board a flight and head to Dubai.The reason? The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are significantly cheaper in the UAE than in India, according to prices cited by Gulf News. And for some buyers, the difference is large enough to make even the cost of flying to Dubai part of the calculation.As the new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max went on sale at the Apple Store in Dubai Mall on September 18, Indian shoppers were among those joining the launch-day crowd. While most customers appeared to be UAE residents, many Indian buyers also travelled to the UAE with the new iPhones on their shopping list.For Mumbai resident Aman Solanki, the maths was simple. He said the phone would still cost him less in Dubai even after adding the cost of his flight and visa.“Even with the flight ticket and visa cost, it is still cheaper for me to buy the phone here in Dubai than compared to India where the additional taxes cause it to be very expensive,” Solanki told Gulf News.“For me, it’s actually about ₹50,000 to ₹60,000 more expensive in India than here. I’m also buying two more phones for family, all iPhone Pro Max, so keeping that in mind I came to Dubai,” he said.The price gap that triggered the tripApple’s UAE starting price for the iPhone 18 Pro is Dh5,099 (approximately ₹133,339), while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at Dh5,499 (approximately ₹1,43,648.56). Both models are available in storage configurations ranging from 256GB to 2TB.In India, the iPhone 18 Pro starts at ₹1,64,900 and the Pro Max at ₹1,79,900.At the exchange rates,, the UAE starting price works out to roughly ₹1.32 lakh for the Pro- around ₹33,000 less than its Indian starting price. For the Pro Max, the UAE price converts to about ₹1.42 lakh, creating a difference of roughly ₹38,000.That difference becomes even more noticeable when more than one phone is being purchased.‘I’m saving around ₹20,000 to ₹30,000’Mohammed Sayed from Kerala was another Indian buyer who compared the two markets before making his purchase.Unlike Solanki, Sayed was already in Dubai to visit family. But after checking the prices, he decided that the new iPhone should come home with him too. “I actually came to visit my family here too but decided to buy the phone here after comparing the cost between UAE and India. For me I’m saving around ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 for the new iPhone. The taxes really increase the price,” he told Gulf News.The new iPhone may have been launched as a smartphone, but for these buyers, the first upgrade was perhaps not the camera or the processor. It was the destination on the boarding pass.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 promo: Rohit Shetty walks out after Avinash Mishra accuses him of doing ‘favours’ for Karan Wahi; says, ‘Mere saath badtameezi nahi’
articles.summary: The latest promo of Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 hints at a heated exchange between Avinash Mishra, Karan Wahi and host Rohit Shetty. What begins as a disagr.
articles.body: The latest promo of Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 hints at a heated exchange between Avinash Mishra, Karan Wahi and host Rohit Shetty. What begins as a disagreement between the contestants soon escalates when Avinash appears to suggest that Rohit is doing favours for Karan. Rohit is visibly upset by the remark and eventually walks out of the set.In the promo, Avinash is seen speaking about the ongoing situation and says, “Karan bhai, aisa ho gaya aajkal ki aur Farrhana ko mujhe nahi hai harana.” (Karan, it has become like this nowadays that I don’t have to defeat Farrhana.)Karan Wahi, seemingly unhappy with the way things are being treated as a joke, responds, “Har cheez ko mazaak, mere ko nahi achha lagta.” (I don’t like everything being turned into a joke.)Avinash then continues, “Theek hai aap purane ho, mere ko farak nahi padta yaar. Hoga, jaante honge. Favour.” (Okay, you are an old contestant, but it doesn’t matter to me. Maybe you know them, maybe you don’t. Favour.)His comment appears to catch Rohit Shetty’s attention. The host asks him what he means by favour and says, “Jaante hain favour matlab? Hello, main favour kar raha hoon main in log pe.” (Do you know what favour means? Hello, am I doing favours for these people?)Rohit then loses his cool and warns Avinash against speaking disrespectfully to him. He says, “Badtameezi mere saath nahi karna bhai. Aise faltu baatein karte hain, dimaag hi sahi kar dete hain.” (Don’t be disrespectful with me. When you say such pointless things, I have to set things straight.)The promo ends with the host walking away from the set. Karan Wahi, who is returning to the show for the third time, had earlier spoken about how every season brings a different kind of pressure despite his previous experience. He also revealed that he became particularly close to Avinash Mishra and Rithvik Dhanjani during the shoot.The promo has also triggered discussion among Khatron Ke Khiladi viewers online. Some viewers felt that Avinash’s comment crossed a line, while others viewed the exchange as part of the intense competitive atmosphere of the show. Fans have also been discussing the equation between Avinash and Karan, with online discussions showing strong interest in both contestants.One section of viewers has previously praised Avinash’s performance and determination on the show, while others have backed Farrhana and other contestants. The latest promo is now giving fans another reason to debate the contestants’ equations as the competition moves forward.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.
